scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Casino was developed in Havana, Cuba in the early 1950s, originating from Cuban Urban Son and Cuban Cha Cha Cha fused with Mambo and Rumba Guaguancó.
Rueda dancing emerged in the late 1950s at the Club Casino Deportivo.
Following the Cuban revolution and emigration, the dance spread to Miami, where Rene Gueits structured a distinct 'disco-like' Miami style in 1994, removing traditional Afro-Cuban elements.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Rueda de Casino functions as a social gathering dance emphasizing community, humor, and shared rhythm.
It is featured in large international flash mobs, television shows like 'Para Bailar', and local social dances.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Couples form a circle (rueda) and dance synchronized figures called out by a dancer inside the circle.
The dance starts from 'al Medio' or 'Guapea'.
Fundamental moves include Dame, Enchufe, Vacila, and Sombrero.
Watch for Dame, Enchufe, Sombrero.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Rene Gueits founded 'Salsa Lovers' in 1994 and structured the Miami style.
Luis Llamo led the 2024 Cuban rueda project 'Retomando el son bailando casino'.
The two primary styles are Cuban-style Rueda and Miami-style Rueda, which removed traditional Afro-Cuban elements.
Derived from Casino, Cuban Son, Cha Cha Cha, Mambo, and Rumba Guaguancó.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Rueda de Casino is parent of Salsa: Rueda de Casino is danced to salsa music and incorporates casino style salsa.
Rueda de Casino is parent of Cuban Son: Casino and Rueda trace direct origins to Cuban Urban Son.
Rueda de Casino is child of Rueda de bachata: A variant adopting the rueda circle concept to bachata music.
